transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um... I guess I'm here because I just can't stop thinking about my face. The left side of it, specifically. It just looks really crooked and messed up to me. 

It's pretty much all I think about. Like, when I'm at work at the warehouse, or if I go out to salsa night, I just feel like everyone is staring at it and noticing how bad it looks. I mean, they tell me they don't see anything when I ask them about it, but... I just can't get it out of my head.
When people tell you that they don't see anything wrong with your face, do you believe that they might be lying to you or hiding the truth from you?

Yeah, I... I guess I do. I don't think they're doing it to be mean, but... I feel like they're just trying to be nice, you know? Like they just don't want to hurt my feelings. 

Because I know what I see in the mirror. It's right there, it's obvious. So when they tell me they don't see anything wrong, I just... I figure they're just saying what they think I want to hear.
If a medical professional or a plastic surgeon were to examine you and confirm with 100% certainty that your face is perfectly symmetrical, would you be able to accept that as the truth?

I don't know. I mean... I'd want to believe them, but it's just so hard. Like I said, I can't stop thinking about it. It's just right there, the left side of my face looking all crooked and messed up. 

Even if a doctor said it was fine, I'd probably still feel like everyone at the warehouse or at salsa night is noticing it. It's like... even when people tell me they don't see anything, my brain just won't let it go. It's all I can focus on.

Because you find yourself thinking about this so much, do you find yourself doing anything to check your face or hide it, such as frequently looking in the mirror or avoiding certain social situations?

Yeah, I do check it a lot. Especially at work. Before I go back out on the inventory floor, I always go into the bathroom to look in the mirror. I just... I keep checking the left side, trying to pull my cap down a certain way to cover it up, or rubbing at the same spot on my cheek, hoping it'll look better. 

I end up doing it for so long sometimes that I'm late getting back. My picking numbers start falling behind, and my boss gets on me about it. But I just can't stop myself from checking.
When you look in the mirror and see this perceived crookedness, do you believe that it is a sign of an underlying medical condition or a physical illness developing in your face?

No, I don't really think it's an illness or a disease or anything like that. I don't think there's a tumor growing or my muscles are failing. It's just... the shape of it. It's just how my face is built, and it looks wrong. I just think it's ugly and crooked, not that I'm sick.

If you consider how strongly you feel about this, would you say that you are completely certain that your face is crooked, or is there a part of you that wonders if your brain might be playing a trick on you?

I honestly don't know. I mean... to me, I'm completely certain it's there. When I look in the mirror, I see it clear as day. It doesn't feel like a trick at all. 

I guess because everyone else tells me I look fine, there's maybe a small part of me that wonders what's going on... but mostly, no. It just feels like I'm looking at my actual face and it's crooked. I can't really see it any other way, even if I try.
